sections.title: Interview bank U04: CUDA and efficient attention

keyTerms.definition: Original practice, role-derived material. Not actual lab questions.
A set of breadth, ladder, analytical, debug, scenario, and critique questions per unit.

recall.question: What is the provenance of this interview bank?
recall.answer: Original practice, role-derived. The questions are not actual lab questions.

keyTerms.definition: Blocking the working set for on-chip reuse; tiled reads beat naive 1024 to 16.
Running (m, l) statistics; merge with the rescale formula.
Tiled exact attention: outer streams K/V, inner streams Q.
Active over max warps; shared memory often the limiter.

recall.question: Define tiling. For a (1024,1024,1024) matmul with 64-wide tiles, how many times is each A element read from HBM vs naive?
recall.answer: Tiling blocks the working set for on-chip reuse. Naive: 1024 reads per A element. Tiled 64-wide: 16.

recall.question: Write the online softmax (m, l) update for a new block.
recall.answer: m' = max(m, m_b), l' = l exp(m-m') + l_b exp(m_b-m').

recall.question: Name the two FlashAttention loops and what each streams.
recall.answer: Outer streams K/V blocks, inner streams Q blocks.

keyTerms.definition: Max of the row seen so far.
Running sum of exp(x - m).
l' = l exp(m-m') + l_b exp(m_b-m') gives the true normalizer.

recall.question: Deep ladder 1 derives the online softmax merge. What are m and l, and what is the merge formula?
recall.answer: m: running row max. l: running sum of exp(x-m). Merge: m'=max(m,m_b), l' = l exp(m-m') + l_b exp(m_b-m'). After blocks [1,2] then [3,100]: m=100, l~1.0.

keyTerms.definition: (T/Br)(T/Bc) tiled steps; 4 on the T=4 toy.
Only (m, l): O(T); scores recomputed in backward.
The suspect when outputs match at T=64 but not T=65.

recall.question: Deep ladder 2 traces FlashAttention on T=4, Br=Bc=2, d=2. How many block pairs run, and what changes vs standard attention?
recall.answer: 4 block pairs. FLOPs O(T^2 d) unchanged; HBM traffic drops from O(T^2) to tiled. Forward stores only (m,l), O(T).

keyTerms.definition: 4 passes over the score matrix per layer on the toy.
The resource (threads, shared, registers) giving fewest blocks per SM.
Blocks per SM over the max; 25% on the toy.

recall.question: Standard attention, T=8192, h=32, fp16, 4 HBM passes over scores. Compute score traffic per layer and the ratio vs Q/K/V/O traffic at n=4096.
256-thread blocks, 32 regs/thread, 48 KB shared/block. SM limits: 2048 threads, 100 KB shared, 65536 regs, 64 warps. What limits occupancy?
recall.answer: By threads: 8 blocks. By shared: 2. By regs: 8. Shared limits: 2 blocks, occupancy 25%.

keyTerms.definition: The bug: l = l + lb drops the exp rescale of old sums.
The test: compare against the reference on blocks with different maxima.

recall.question: D1. The tiled softmax below is wrong. What is the bug, the fix, and the test that catches it?
recall.answer: Bug: l = l + lb drops the rescale: old sums were normalized to the old max. Fix: track m_new first, then l = l exp(m-m_new) + lb exp(mb-m_new). Test: two-pass reference on blocks like [1,2],[3,100].

keyTerms.definition: One block covers the matrix; loops collapse to a single pass.
The gate for sparse attention: accuracy at max distance within budget.
Start exact (FlashAttention), then test approximate options.

recall.question: SRAM is infinite. How do you redesign attention, and is there any reason to keep tiling?
recall.answer: One block covers the whole matrix: loops collapse, traffic drops to one read of Q,K,V and one write of O. Keep tiling only for parallelism across SMs, not memory.

recall.question: The error budget allows 1% relative error on a long-range retrieval task. Which of sparse w=256, low-rank r=256, FlashAttention do you pick, and what gates it?
recall.answer: Start with FlashAttention (no risk), then test sparse gated on a distance-stratified retrieval eval: sparse ships only if accuracy at max distance stays within budget.

keyTerms.definition: Is the baseline FlashAttention-2 at its best config?
Which T regime? Short-T-only invalidates the claim.

recall.question: A paper claims a new attention variant is “2x faster than FlashAttention-2 with identical outputs.” What five audit questions do you ask?
recall.answer: (1) Same shapes/dtype/hardware and synced timing? (2) Baseline at best config? (3) Identical outputs measured how? (4) Which T regime? (5) Independent reproduction script?
